The date in the register (1977) diverges from 1975 in the description, Wikidata and OSM — 1977 probably relates to publication or acceptance.

buildings.history: The building was erected in 1903–1905 to a design by Alexander Ozerov for the Third Tiflis Women's Gymnasium. The school grew out of a private boarding school opened in 1881 and officially numbered in 1894. The heritage register gives 1903, the year the foundation was laid; the building opened in January 1905. The gymnasium was closed in 1921, and the Sixth Author’s School now occupies the building.

buildings.description: A corner brick house of the early 20th century on the southern slope, its main eastern façade facing Lebanidze Street. The composition is symmetrical: a slightly projecting central risalit with three pairs of openings, a balcony with a metal railing and a segmental pediment above the cornice, framed by a crenellated parapet of kongury. The decoration is restrained for Art Nouveau: stucco garlands and wreaths, square frieze panels, faceted architraves; all the openings are rectangular and deeply recessed into the wall. In the vestibule there survive a marble two-flight staircase, mosaic floors and relief panels, including a composition with Adam and Eve and oval medallions with a female figure.

In the vestibule the authentic reliefs are covered by modern thermal insulation panels, the courtyard's open galleries have been entirely built in, and the original gates have been replaced.

The house and printing press were restored in 1937, and a museum opened in the restored house. The register dates the house to the early 20th century and describes its gallery, wooden balcony, and entrance to the underground rooms. A separate, larger museum building was constructed in the yard in the mid-20th century. The map shows the address-matched one-storey house, OSM way/478568522; the official heritage boundary covers the wider site, courtyard, and museum building.

The arcades consist of two blocks: one is separated from the Artsruni caravanserai, the second is perceived as the boundary between Bambis Rigi and Shardeni (the former Dark Row); in the atlas these are two separate cards.

The authors were the architects Leopold Bielfeld and Alexander Rogoisky; the main block was largely finished by 1903, and the bell tower marked with a red line on the drawing was never built. After the Sovietisation of Georgia in 1921 the seminary was closed, a military school was housed here, in 1929 an agricultural institute, and from 1967 the 9th city hospital; later the building was occupied by the institute for the advanced training of physicians. In 2007, with the blessing of Patriarch Ilia II, the Church of Saint Andrew the First-Called was restored in the building.

buildings.description: The first building of Tbilisi State University on Chavchavadze Avenue, 1–3 was built in 1900–1916 to a design by Simon Kldiashvili. It was conceived as a university, but under the Russian Empire permission was granted only for a nobility school; in 1918 the university opened here.
buildings.history: Construction began in 1900; by 1906 part of the building housed a Georgian gymnasium, and the corps was completed only in 1916. In 1918 the university was founded here and was then the only one in the Caucasus.

buildings.description: The Tbilisi TV Broadcasting Tower was built in 1972 on Mount Mtatsminda. It is 274.5 metres high and is one of the city’s main vertical landmarks.
buildings.history: The tower replaced the previous 1955 TV tower, which was moved to the Gori area. Since 1972 it has provided television and radio broadcasting for Tbilisi; a 1994 fire damaged the upper structures, and the tower was subsequently repaired.

buildings.history: The building of the G. Mikeladze Republican Scientific and Technical Library opened in 1985 to a design by the architect Gari Bichiashvili. The library held technical literature, patents, drawings and standards, and before the spread of the internet was one of the main information centres for engineers. In 2006 the library became part of the National Scientific Library of Georgia.

buildings.history: The new TSU campus in the Vere valley was designed in 1968–1970; the 1970 general plan was produced by a team led by Zurab Kopaladze. The library for five million books was completed in 1971 to a design by Shota Kachkachishvili, Zurab Kopaladze, Bidzina Maminaishvili, Nodar Mgaloblishvili, Aleksandre Sabashvili and Devi Chopikashvili. The campus was to include academic buildings, dormitories, a sports zone and a bridge over the Vere; construction stopped in 1989 and some structures remained unfinished. The library still serves as the university’s central library.

buildings.description: A thirteen-storey university tower: a long slab with a regular window grid and vertical ribs, set on a low podium at the edge of the Vere gorge. The main facade faces University Street, the side elevations are more closed; a broad stair leads to the entrance. The building is the main vertical landmark of the new university campus.
buildings.history: Building 10 (Maghlivi) was constructed in 1968 to a design by Shota Kachkachishvili, Mikheil Shavishvili, S. Bezhanov and M. Shubladze — before the 1970 general plan for the new campus was approved. That plan envisaged a campus of about 240 hectares in the Vere valley, with academic buildings, a library, dormitories, a sports zone and a bridge over the river; construction stopped in 1989. The building is still used by the university.
